transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Eli Turner (MapleHealth CTO), Maya Chen (MapleHealth Sr PM), Ravi Patel (MapleHealth ML Eng)
Notes: demo deck + quick hosted walkthrough; security/POC next steps

[00:00] Jordan Blake: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan, i'm the ae on the account. quick check, you can hear us okay?
[00:06] Eli Turner: yeah loud and clear, thanks jordan. we got priya and jordan, thanks for squeezing us in.
[00:12] Priya Nair: hi team, priya here, i'll do the live part of the demo and answer infra and perf q's.
[00:18] Maya Chen: great. our aim is to evaluate a hosted flow for clinician chat summarization and triage, low latency preferred but cost matters.
[00:25] Jordan Blake: perfect, that matches what we thought. quick agenda: 1) quick product primer 2) live Conversation API demo with streaming 3) parameter tuning and retry/backoff patterns 4) console and Optimize suggestions 5) q&a / next steps. sound ok?
[00:36] Eli Turner: yep let's go.
[00:40] Priya Nair: i'll start by showing a simple chat gen call. first thing: streaming. when you stream, the API yields deltas as tokens come out, so your UI can render progressively and keep latency low.
[00:52] [00:52] Priya Nair: (demo) sending a request... here you see the events: partial text, token indexes, and a final event. on the SDK side that's simply an async iterator.
[01:02] Ravi Patel: quick q — does streaming maintain token ordering if we do retries? we sometimes have flaky mobile connections.
[01:08] Priya Nair: good call. by default we recommend idempotency keys for non-streaming calls; for streaming we surface resumable tokens for some model variants — basically you can rehydrate the KV cache and resume if a connection drops, but it's model-dependent. we'll share the KB link in follow-up.
[01:22] Maya Chen: is resumability available on hosted tier or only on dedicated?
[01:27] Priya Nair: resumability is available on hosted for our newer verified models; for heavy production you might prefer Dedicated for stricter SLOs and pinned capacity, but hosted works for most use cases.
[01:36] [01:36] Jordan Blake: quick qualification: what qps and typical conversation length are you expecting?
[01:42] Eli Turner: at peak maybe 120 qps across all services, average chat ~120 tokens per response, sometimes longer for summaries.
[01:50] Jordan Blake: got it — that helps sizing. on pricing that sits comfortably in hosted for sure but we can run burst tests.
[01:56] [01:56] Priya Nair: now parameter tuning. temperature and top_p: set temperature low (0.0-0.3) for deterministic summaries. max_tokens should set a safe cap—use the stream to detect early termination. we also recommend stop sequences to avoid run-on.
[02:12] Ravi Patel: about stop sequences: we have structured outputs with JSON blobs, any tips?
[02:16] Priya Nair: use functions / structured output support; enforce schemas on the client side but also prefer few-shot examples plus stop to reduce hallucinations. for JSON use trailing delimiter and validate.
[02:28] [02:28] (audio glitches)
[02:31] Maya Chen: sorry, slight echo.
[02:33] Jordan Blake: no worries. switching to retries/backoff — common pattern: client should do exponential backoff with jitter. Redwood supports 429 and 5xx codes with recommended Retry-After headers. we also have a small client middleware you can drop into your SDK to handle the logic.
[02:50] Eli Turner: do you provide token-level accounting or per-request cost estimates? we need that for our finance folks.
[02:57] Priya Nair: yes, Console shows token breakdown per request and per-route. You can also tag requests by route to get cost by feature. we'll show the console in a bit.
[03:06] [03:06] Priya Nair: now a live demo — sending a chat request with streaming and temperature 0.1, max_tokens 300. watch the partial tokens come through.
[03:16] (demo typing noises)
[03:18] Speaker 1: so there's a token chunk, and another.
[03:22] Priya Nair: you might notice the partial chunks sometimes include punctuation splits — that's expected. if you need character-level UX smoothing we recommend a simple buffer and flushing strategy on the client.
[03:34] Ravi Patel: if the mobile disconnects after partials, can we replay the partials for the user and then resume?
[03:39] Priya Nair: yes — two approaches: 1) keep the partial stream and show partials as provisional; 2) persist last n tokens server-side (we do prefix caching options) then resume with a new request that uses prefix. resume complexity increases slightly but it's doable.
[03:52] [03:52] Jordan Blake: quick aside on caching: our Optimize tool suggests prefix caching when you have repetitive prompts — that can cut per-token spend.
[03:59] Maya Chen: how does caching interact with PII? our transcripts have PHI.
[04:04] Priya Nair: for PHI you can opt out of caching and configure retention to zero on hosted, or choose Private deployment where you control keys and retention. also Redwood integrates with KMS for envelope encryption.
[04:15] Eli Turner: do you support bringing your own KMS?
[04:18] Priya Nair: yes — BYOK via customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports integration with cloud KMS for key encryptions. we'll include the architecture diagram.
[04:28] [04:28] Jordan Blake: moving to console — i'll share my screen. first, per-route charts: latency P50/P95, tokens per request, and cost. you can create rate limits and automatic fallback policies to lower-cost model variants.
[04:40] Maya Chen: can fallbacks be region-aware? we have data residency in eu-west.
[04:44] Priya Nair: yes, routing policies can be region and tier aware; you can set fallbacks to a quantized variant in same region.
[04:50] [04:50] (short silence)
[04:53] Priya Nair: now Optimize suggestions — for your workload we'd recommend: 1) batching small requests into microbatch windows of 50-200ms during non-interactive flows; 2) prefix caching for repeated system prompts; 3) try an 8-bit quantized variant for cost reductions on background summarization jobs.
[05:09] Ravi Patel: regarding quantization — what are the expected quality regressions? we're sensitive for clinician outputs.
[05:15] Priya Nair: Optimize provides quality-vs-cost tradeoff reports based on your prompt set. For summaries you might see minor token-choice differences; we can run a short eval on your prompt set during the POC to measure ROUGE/semantic drift.
[05:28] [05:28] Jordan Blake: competitor question: how are we different from Vertex AI/Anthropic?
[05:33] Priya Nair: short answer: unified runtime focused on inference economics and production ops — streaming-first primitives, smart routing across hosting/dedicated/private, and deep observability at token level. Vertex is more infra + mdoel hosting; Anthropic has different model family and safety focus — for you the key is the production controls (fallbacks, quotas, SLOs).
[05:52] Maya Chen: thanks — can you send a short one-pager comparing the options?
[05:55] Jordan Blake: yep will do.
[05:58] [05:58] (demo interruption)
[06:00] Priya Nair: walking through a retry example: client does exponential backoff and if request fails after x attempts, Redwood can fallback to a lighter model variant automatically if configured. that keeps UX alive.
[06:11] Eli Turner: what's the harm of automatic fallback for us — could it produce worse outputs?
[06:16] Priya Nair: it can, so we recommend canarying and using content checks to verify critical fields. Redwood also supports automatic rollback and A/B variants so you can test fallback impacts.
[06:29] Ravi Patel: latency numbers — what's P95 hosted for conversational model at 16 tokens?
[06:33] Priya Nair: across our regions P95 for typical chat is 180-350ms for verified medium models; for long sequences it increases. Dedicated gives tighter tails with reserved GPUs. we'll attach recent perf spreadsheet.
[06:47] [06:47] Maya Chen: curious about tokenization differences; we saw token counts vary across vendors and it changes cost.
[06:52] Priya Nair: yes tokenization differs — Console token counts are normalized by model. for cost forecasts we use model-specific tokenizers in our billing pipeline.
[07:01] [07:01] Jordan Blake: quick pricing note: hosted billing is per-token and per-embedding unit; we can provide monthly estimate given your qps and average tokens. reserved Dedicated capacity is monthly commit with lower per-token unit economics.
[07:14] Maya Chen: do you have an SLA for hosted?
[07:17] Priya Nair: hosted has an uptime target but enterprise-grade SLA is on Dedicated. hosted still has strong reliability and fallbacks.
[07:25] [07:25] (screen scroll)
[07:27] Priya Nair: back to streaming UX — implementation tips: buffer small partials for 50-100ms, merge tokens to avoid flicker, and surface a spinner if the stream stalls for >500ms. for interactive chat low buffer sizes lower latency but increase jitter.
[07:42] Ravi Patel: regarding SDKs — node and python? mobile?
[07:46] Priya Nair: official SDKs node, python, and a lightweight JS streaming helper for browsers and RN. mobile clients typically use a gateway microservice to manage tokens and resume logic.
[07:58] [07:58] Jordan Blake: security deep-dive questions — maya, you mentioned PHI; anything specific like BAA requirements?
[08:04] Maya Chen: yes we need BAA and SOC2 Type II, and audit logs for data access. also SAML SSO for our admins.
[08:11] Priya Nair: noted — Redwood offers SOC2 Type II reports, audit logs, SAML/SSO, RBAC, and can sign a BAA for Private/Dedicated deployments. hosted customers often want Private for strict PHI controls.
[08:23] Eli Turner: timeline — we'd like to pilot in september. is that feasible?
[08:27] Jordan Blake: yes — we recommended POC kickoff first week of september. we'll run a week-long bench with your prompt set and a small integration test.
[08:35] [08:35] (brief pause)
[08:37] Priya Nair: demo wrap: sending an example with streaming + stop sequences to show deterministic output.
[08:44] (demo)
[08:47] Speaker 2: output arrives, structure preserved, good.
[08:51] Maya Chen: nice.
[08:53] Jordan Blake: last section: Console alerts and dashboards — you can set cost thresholds, token anomalies, and evaluation regressions. Optimize will trigger a regression alert if a model variant drops below baseline on your test prompts.
[09:07] Ravi Patel: would you run an eval for us during POC? we'll share the prompt set.
[09:11] Priya Nair: yes — Optimize can run spot evals and generate a quality vs cost report. we'll include that in the POC scope.
[09:20] [09:20] Jordan Blake: open floor for questions.
[09:23] Maya Chen: what logs will we get if we go hosted—full transcripts or redacted?
[09:27] Priya Nair: hosted stores transcripts by default but you can configure retention and redaction; for PHI we recommend disabling retention and using Private or encrypted logging.
[09:38] Eli Turner: who owns the network egress — we need VPC peering?
[09:42] Priya Nair: for Private we deploy into your VPC; for Dedicated we support private connectivity; hosted uses TLS with optional customer-managed endpoints for some customers. we'll provide the network diagram.
[09:54] [09:54] (typing, link paste)
[09:56] Jordan Blake: sharing links — SOC2 pack, perf spreadsheet, and hosted vs dedicated one-pager.
[09:59] Maya Chen: thanks. one last q on throttling — if we exceed qps, how graceful is degradation?
[10:05] Priya Nair: two layers: client-side backoff and server-side rate limiting. we also auto-fallback to a cheaper variant if you opt in. in practice it keeps user-facing errors low.
[10:16] Ravi Patel: okay, that's helpful.
[10:19] [10:19] Jordan Blake: recap and next steps — we'll send the docs, pricing, SOC2, and schedule the POC kickoff for first week of september. Jordan to own pricing, Priya to own security pack, Ravi to share prompts.
[10:32] Maya Chen: sounds good. thanks all.
[10:35] Eli Turner: appreciated.
[10:37] Priya Nair: thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the benchmark script.
[10:42] Jordan Blake: end meeting.

End transcript.
